entity.name: Tejas Prasad
entity.description: Independent security researcher and open-source developer building runtime behavioral analysis tools to secure software supply chains. Author of published research on cascading API vulnerabilities and maintainer of TraceTree and Switchboard-MCP.

projects.name: TraceTree
projects.description: Local-first runtime behavioral analysis tool and sandbox that maps package execution and MCP tool calls into directed graphs to detect supply-chain attacks. Instead of relying on signatures, it records what a package actually does at runtime (file, network, process and syscall activity) and flags malicious behavior patterns.

channels.description: Direct bank wire or UPI transfer upon grant approval (contact via email)

plans.name: Core Sandbox & Behavioral Detection Engine
plans.description: 12 months of focused maintenance and development: cross-platform syscall tracing (extending beyond Linux eBPF to macOS and Windows), expanding and tuning the malicious-behavior detection rules to reduce false positives, an independent security review of the sandbox itself, test infrastructure, and comprehensive documentation for open-source maintainers adopting TraceTree.

plans.name: MCP Tool-Call Scanning & CI Integration
plans.description: Extends TraceTree to scan MCP servers and tool calls for malicious behavior, adds a shareable rule format so the community can contribute detections, and ships a GitHub Actions integration so maintainers can vet dependencies automatically in CI.
